slice.target: Cargo --offline network behavior combined with the already-verified vendored source-replacement subclaim

public_source.scope: cargo(1) general command options, especially --offline and --frozen

slice.finding: The official cargo(1) page states that --offline prevents Cargo itself from accessing the network and makes Cargo proceed using locally available data when possible; it also states that --frozen combines --locked with --offline. Combined with the immediately preceding role-local finding that crates.io can be replaced by a checked-in vendored directory source, this closes the narrow Cargo-internal network-access subclaim for dependency resolution/build orchestration when all required dependency data is already local.
slice.verified_scope: Cargo's own network access can be disabled with --offline; when required dependency data is locally available, including via the previously verified directory source-replacement pattern, Cargo can attempt dependency resolution/build orchestration without Cargo network access.
not_verified_scope: Whether package build scripts, proc-macros, compiler wrappers, or other subprocesses spawned during a build can independently access the network.
Whether every dependency class is fully satisfiable from the chosen vendored/source-replacement layout without additional local cache/index material.
Whether scheduled Chat can execute Cargo or rustc at all.

scope_guard: Do not broaden Cargo's documented --offline guarantee into a claim that arbitrary build subprocesses are network-isolated, or into a claim that Chat can execute Cargo. The finding closes only Cargo-internal network access under locally satisfiable inputs.
exact_continuation: On the next invocation, fresh-bootstrap and freeze current authority, then inspect exactly one official Cargo/Rust documentation page addressing build scripts or spawned build-time processes. Determine only whether Cargo --offline constrains those subprocesses' independent network access; if it does not, record that hidden-network side effect as a remaining blocker without broadening to actual Cargo execution.
